# 1:1 — Wei (Manager) and Theo (Frontend Engineer)

**Attendees:** Wei (EM), Theo (Senior Frontend Engineer)

---

Wei: Hey Theo. How's it going? Anything heavy on your mind before we get into the agenda?

Theo: One thing — I've been thinking about the conversation we had last quarter about staff-track vs management-track. I'm leaning more strongly toward staff. I want to talk through what the next twelve months look like.

Wei: Good, let's spend most of the time on that. Anything urgent on the sprint side first?

Theo: The permissions-screen accessibility audit is booked for Thursday next week. I'm a little worried that Priya's copy isn't finalized yet, which could delay the audit.

Wei: I talked to Felix this morning. Priya commits to Wednesday end of day. If she misses, we push the audit to the following week. I'll handle that scheduling — you don't need to chase it.

Theo: Thanks.

Wei: OK, staff track. Tell me what's drawing you toward it versus management.

Theo: Two things. First, the work that energizes me is hard technical problems where I can spend extended time deep in code. The pair programming with Ana last sprint was the most engaged I've felt in months. Management work feels more like switching cost, less like flow. Second, I've watched you and Mei do management and I respect the work, but I don't see myself reaching for it the same way.

Wei: That's a clear signal. What does the next twelve months look like for you to make staff?

Theo: I want to be the technical lead on a multi-team initiative. The settings refresh is a candidate, but I'd want it to be cross-team — frontend, backend, design — not just frontend.

Wei: I think that's the right scope. I'll talk to Priya and Yusuf about expanding the settings refresh charter to include data-model changes — that pulls Ana in formally. If they agree, I'll designate you as the technical lead. I'll have that conversation by next week's leadership sync.

Theo: That would be great.

Wei: Beyond the lead role, what else? Staff calibration looks at influence, not just delivery. You'll want a few visible cross-team artifacts. A couple of options: lead a tech-talk series, write up a post on the pair-programming pattern that worked, take on a hiring-loop interviewer slot.

Theo: I'll take the pair-programming write-up. I can have a draft ready in two weeks for your review.

Wei: Done. And the hiring loop?

Theo: Yes, I'll volunteer for the next senior frontend role. Lin can put me on the rotation.

Wei: I'll send Lin a note today asking to add you. The tech-talk series I'll let you decide on later — don't pile on.

Theo: One concern — performance reviews are coming up. Will the staff-track conversation factor into this cycle's review or is it forward-looking only?

Wei: This cycle is on your existing senior-engineer rubric. The staff-track milestones I described — lead role, write-up, interviewer slot — those land in the next cycle's evaluation. So expect this December review to look like a strong senior, and next December's review to evaluate against staff criteria.

Theo: That's clear. Thanks.

Wei: Last thing from me — I noticed you've been working late on Wednesdays for the last three weeks. Is something blocking you, or is that personal preference?

Theo: It's the design handoffs landing late. I lose Tuesday afternoon waiting for a clean spec, then catch up Wednesday evening. It's not sustainable.

Wei: I'll raise this with Priya when I talk about the settings refresh charter. I'd rather we shift the handoff cadence than have you absorb the cost. Don't burn yourself out — flag this earlier next time.

Theo: Will do.

Wei: Recap. I talk to Priya and Yusuf about expanding the settings refresh to a cross-team charter and designating you as technical lead, by next week's leadership sync. I send Lin a note today adding you to the hiring rotation. I raise the late-handoff cadence with Priya. You draft the pair-programming write-up in two weeks for my review. Performance review this cycle uses the senior rubric; staff calibration is next cycle.

Theo: Got it.

Wei: Same time next week?

Theo: See you then.
